title: Soundness of the Numeric Checks
statement: Let $M$ be a finite Turing machine with Boolean input alphabet, let $x$ be a Boolean string, let $W$ be a natural number, let $\mathrm{Ans}$ assign a Boolean value to each selector and pair of natural-number indices, and let $xb$ be a Boolean-valued function on the natural numbers. Suppose that for every $t<2^W$, $a<2^W$, and $j\le |x|+1$, every prescribed initialization, transition, work-tape, input, boundary, and final check is satisfied by the numerical encoding determined by $\mathrm{Ans}$ and $xb$. Suppose also that $xb(j)=x_j$ for every $j<|x|$. Then after $2^W-1$ steps, the machine $M$ is halted and its output register records exactly one bit, equal to $1$.
hypotheses_covered: $M$ is a finite Turing machine with Boolean alphabet
$\mathrm{Ans}$ is a Boolean-valued function on selectors and two natural-number indices
All prescribed checks hold for every $t<2^W$, $a<2^W$, and $j\le |x|+1$
caveat: The check predicate is defined by a detailed encoding and a finite family of local Boolean constraints; the supplied descriptions do not explain these constraints informally.
